title: Industrial ReMEmbR: Scaling Spatiotemporal Memory to Robot Fleets
why_read: A practical systems paper on scaling shared robot memory across fleets while handling privacy, bandwidth, and compute constraints, relevant to applied robotics engineers.
analysis: This paper extends NVIDIA's ReMEmbR memory system to warehouse robot fleets, addressing the real engineering problem of how to store and query video-derived knowledge without transmitting raw camera footage. It splits a vision-language model so the vision encoder runs on-robot (on Jetson hardware) and the language decoder runs on a server, generating scene descriptions only when queried to save compute. It also folds in privacy features like blurring detected people for GDPR compliance. This is a good example of applied systems engineering for multi-robot deployments rather than a fundamental research advance.
